subsystems.name: Core Mapping Engine
subsystems.description: AutoMapper's Core Mapping Engine is the heart of the library: it defines the public configuration DSL (CreateMap, ForMember, ForCtorParam), stores mapping metadata in TypeMap, compiles each TypeMap into an executable delegate via TypeMapPlanBuilder, and exposes the runtime IMapper facade. It also owns the exception model (AutoMapperMappingException and AutoMapperConfigurationException), the per-map ResolutionContext, the feature-extension mechanism in Features.cs, and the DI registration helpers in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs. The subsystem exists as a separate unit because it separates the two fundamentally different phases of AutoMapper: declarative configuration can be validated and compiled up front, while the generated expression trees are then executed repeatedly at runtime; keeping these phases apart lets profiles be defined independently and lets the plan builder optimize mapping code. Data flows from user profiles through Profile's CreateMap (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/Profile.cs:149) into MapperConfiguration's constructor (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/MapperConfiguration.cs:67), which resolves TypeMaps via GetTypeMap (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/MapperConfiguration.cs:350) and compiles them with BuildExecutionPlan (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/MapperConfiguration.cs:210) and TypeMapPlanBuilder.CreateMapperLambda (src/AutoMapper/Execution/TypeMapPlanBuilder.cs:40); at runtime Mapper.MapCore (src/AutoMapper/Mapper.cs:192) uses ResolutionContext (src/AutoMapper/ResolutionContext.cs:12) to execute those delegates. It connects to the neighbouring Mapper Registry and Queryable Projection subsystems through related files such as the validator, conventions, ExpressionBuilder, and ProjectionBuilder, while its DI-facing surface is exercised by the AutoMapper.DI.Tests project and the licensing files validate editions before mapping is enabled.

files.role: Defines the exception types thrown when configuration or mapping fails. These exceptions wrap type-map errors and preserve a list of configuration errors, giving callers a stable failure surface.

key_symbols.explanation: Top-level runtime exception that wraps any error raised while a mapping is being executed.

key_symbols.name: AutoMapperConfigurationException
key_symbols.explanation: Configuration-time exception used when type maps or profiles are invalid, carrying a list of TypeMapConfigErrors.

key_symbols.name: ForMember

key_symbols.name: IMappingExpressionBase

key_symbols.name: ForCtorParam
key_symbols.explanation: Configures a constructor parameter mapping in a type-agnostic way.

files.role: Defines per-operation options passed to a Map call, including service construction and before/after map callbacks. MappingOperationOptions provides the concrete implementation used by the runtime mapper.

key_symbols.explanation: Interface describing options for a single Map operation.

key_symbols.name: CreateMap

subsystems.name: Mapper Registry
subsystems.description: Mapper Registry is the subsystem that collects, validates, and indexes all type maps and supplies the built-in object mappers used for primitive, collection, enum, nullable, string, and dynamic conversions. It exists as a distinct unit because mapping between arbitrary type pairs cannot be solved by user-declared TypeMaps alone: AutoMapper needs a deterministic ordering of built-in strategies that can decide whether a pair is assignable, enumerable, convertible, or parseable, and then generate an expression. The flow begins with MapperConfigurationExpression's AddMapsCore (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/MapperConfigurationExpression.cs:176), which registers profiles and maps; ProfileMap.Register (src/AutoMapper/ProfileMap.cs:124) and BuildTypeMap (src/AutoMapper/ProfileMap.cs:140) build the TypeMaps, and ConfigurationValidator.AssertConfigurationIsValid (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/ConfigurationValidator.cs:23) verifies them. At runtime, when no user type map applies, MapperConfiguration asks MapperRegistry's Mappers collection (src/AutoMapper/Mappers/MapperRegistry.cs:5) to find a mapper whose IsMatch and MapExpression contract (src/AutoMapper/Mappers/IObjectMapper.cs:12, src/AutoMapper/Mappers/IObjectMapper.cs:24) can produce the conversion. ExpressionBuilder.MapExpression (src/AutoMapper/Execution/ExpressionBuilder.cs:63) assembles sub-expressions for nested maps. This ties into the Core Mapping Engine via MapperConfiguration, TypeMapPlanBuilder, and TypeMap, and its related files show consumers in DI tests and attribute configuration that rely on the registry to create and validate maps.

subsystems.name: Attribute Configuration
subsystems.description: Attribute Configuration lets mapping rules be declared as .NET attributes on the model types themselves rather than imperatively in a profile. It exists as a separate subsystem because AutoMapper's API intentionally offers two configuration styles, code-first profiles and metadata-driven attributes, and the attribute layer isolates the reflection and discovery logic behind a common IMemberConfigurationProvider contract. Each attribute's ApplyConfiguration method (e.g. src/AutoMapper/Configuration/Annotations/AutoMapAttribute.cs:48) receives the mapping or member configuration expression and mutates it; the member-level attributes such as IgnoreAttribute, MapAtRuntimeAttribute, MappingOrderAttribute, NullSubstituteAttribute, SourceMemberAttribute, UseExistingValueAttribute, ValueConverterAttribute, and ValueResolverAttribute all implement that same ApplyConfiguration hook. The entry point is IMemberConfigurationExpression (src/AutoMapper/Configuration/IMemberConfigurationExpression.cs:9), the interface through which attributes specify MapFrom, conditions, ordering, null substitution, value converters and resolvers, and destination-value behavior. This subsystem connects to the Core Mapping Engine through Profile, MappingExpression, and MemberConfigurationExpression, and to TypeMapPlanBuilder so that attribute-declared resolvers and converters end up in generated mapping plans; its tests live in UnitTests and integration test projects.

subsystems.name: Queryable Projection
subsystems.description: Queryable Projection translates AutoMapper mapping rules into LINQ expression trees that can execute in a query provider, typically producing a Select call for EF or LINQ to SQL. It exists as a separate subsystem because in-memory mapping can already be performed by compiled delegates, but translating to IQueryable requires building expression trees from TypeMaps, rewriting member accesses for null-safety, and avoiding client-side evaluation. The flow starts from Extensions.ProjectTo (src/AutoMapper/QueryableExtensions/Extensions.cs:34), which calls ProjectionBuilder.CreateProjection (src/AutoMapper/QueryableExtensions/ProjectionBuilder.cs:72); CreateProjection uses projection requests and let-property maps to manage subqueries and depth, and NullsafeQueryRewriter (src/AutoMapper/QueryableExtensions/NullsafeQueryRewriter.cs:36) rewrites potentially null chains into conditional expressions. Leaf conversions are delegated to projection mappers such as EnumerableProjectionMapper (src/AutoMapper/QueryableExtensions/ProjectionMappers/EnumerableProjectionMapper.cs:11) and StringProjectionMapper (src/AutoMapper/QueryableExtensions/ProjectionMappers/StringProjectionMapper.cs:7), while ObjectFactory (src/AutoMapper/Execution/ObjectFactory.cs:21) and ProxyGenerator (src/AutoMapper/Execution/ProxyGenerator.cs:20) create constructor and proxy expressions used by the results. LockingConcurrentDictionary (src/AutoMapper/Internal/LockingConcurrentDictionary.cs:4) caches compiled projections. It connects to the Core Mapping Engine via MapperConfiguration, TypeMap, ProfileMap, and MemberMap, and to ExpressionBuilder and TypeMapPlanBuilder for shared expression-building utilities.

subsystems.name: Licensing Types
subsystems.description: Licensing Types is the smallest subsystem in the repository and defines the ProductType type (src/AutoMapper/Licensing/ProductType.cs:3) that identifies which AutoMapper product edition a license key covers. It exists as a separate unit so the licensing product model is isolated from the mapping engine's core types; changing the set of editions or their public names should not ripple through mapping code. The type flows into the licensing pipeline through LicenseAccessor's initialization and validation (src/AutoMapper/Licensing/LicenseAccessor.cs:29) and LicenseValidator's checks (src/AutoMapper/Licensing/LicenseValidator.cs:21), which decide whether a valid unrestricted license is present before the mapper accepts the configuration. There are no captured related files for this cluster, but the sibling licensing files in src/AutoMapper/Licensing form the enclosing subsystem that consumes this type.

files.role: Defines the product edition identifiers used by license validation. It is a standalone domain type whose values are interpreted by the license key validation pipeline.

key_symbols.name: ProductType
key_symbols.explanation: Represents the product editions a license key can be issued for.

subsystems.name: Benchmark Utilities
subsystems.description: This subsystem provides a dedicated high-resolution timer for benchmarking operations in the repository. It wraps the Windows performance-counter API so callers can measure elapsed time with sub-millisecond precision instead of relying on coarser wall-clock timers. It exists as its own unit because the P/Invoke declarations and the underlying counter plumbing are platform-specific and would otherwise clutter application code; isolating them in one class lets every benchmark share the same measurement path. Control flows from the caller through HiPerfTimer's constructor, which initializes the timing frequency, then Start() captures a starting performance-counter value, and Stop() captures the ending value. The difference between those two samples, combined with the frequency obtained by the constructor, yields the elapsed time. The class declares QueryPerformanceCounter at src/Benchmark/HiPerfTimer.cs:7 and QueryPerformanceFrequency at src/Benchmark/HiPerfTimer.cs:11, and uses them inside HiPerfTimer at src/Benchmark/HiPerfTimer.cs:19, Start at src/Benchmark/HiPerfTimer.cs:32, and Stop at src/Benchmark/HiPerfTimer.cs:41. It has no listed related files, so it currently connects only to whatever benchmark code instantiates HiPerfTimer rather than to another subsystem.

files.role: This file defines the high-resolution timer used for measuring benchmarks. It encapsulates the Windows performance-counter API and exposes a minimal Start/Stop interface for callers.

key_symbols.name: Start
key_symbols.explanation: Captures a starting performance-counter sample; callers invoke it immediately before the code being benchmarked.

key_symbols.name: Stop
key_symbols.explanation: Captures an ending performance-counter sample; callers invoke it immediately after the code being benchmarked.

key_symbols.name: QueryPerformanceFrequency
key_symbols.explanation: P/Invoke declaration for the Win32 function that supplies how many counter ticks occur per second.

subsystems.name: Assembly Metadata
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the assembly metadata declaration for the TestApp project. Its single file contains the CLR attributes that describe the compiled assembly, such as version, title, product, and culture information. It exists as a separate unit because .NET tooling and project templates keep assembly-wide attributes in a dedicated Properties file, which prevents application entry-point code from being mixed with build metadata. There is no runtime control or data flow: the compiler reads the attributes during compilation and embeds them into the assembly manifest. In that sense the flow is build-time metadata from this file directly into TestApp's output, rather than through any function. Because this item's related_files list is empty, it does not call into or get imported by other subsystems; it stands as static input consumed only by the compiler.

files.role: This file stores assembly-level metadata attributes for TestApp. It is read by the compiler at build time and does not participate in application runtime behavior.

overview.description: AutoMapper is a .NET object-object mapping library that separates declarative configuration from compiled runtime execution, with the Core Mapping Engine at its center managing profiles, type maps, validation, and the generated mapping delegates. The Mapper Registry supports that engine by supplying built-in object mappers for primitive, collection, enum, nullable, string, and dynamic conversions when no user-defined type map applies. Attribute Configuration offers an alternative configuration style by letting mapping rules be declared as metadata on model types and fed through the same mapping-expression pipeline into generated plans. Queryable Projection extends the system to IQueryable sources by translating mapping rules into expression trees suitable for query providers such as EF. The remaining pieces are peripheral: Licensing Types guards whether the mapper can be used, while Benchmark Utilities and Assembly Metadata exist only for repository tooling and test-app build metadata, not for mapping behavior.
